#### The watermark generator — stack and heap at every step

**What is being answered.** Why the watermark formula contains `max()`, by running both formulas over the same stream and counting what goes wrong.

`naiveWatermark(e)` is `e.et - LAG` — the version that looks equivalent. `correctWatermark(seen, e)` adds one line. `run(useMax)` generates both and counts any value lower than its predecessor.

The counts are 2 and 0. Step 4 then shows why that matters: a regression takes window 0, which had already fired and published, back to "not yet complete". Monotonicity is not tidiness — it is the property every downstream trigger assumes.

The animation steps through the code, holding each line long enough to read the STACK (call frames and their locals) and the HEAP (allocated arrays and objects) as they are AT THAT MOMENT. Expand any step to study it on its own.

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch03-system-memory/ch03-system-memory.svg" alt="The watermark generator — stack and heap at every step, 4 steps showing stack and heap" width="980">

<details>
<summary><b>Step 1 of 4</b> — the naive formula reads only the CURRENT event</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch03-system-memory/frames/step-01.svg" alt="Step 1: the naive formula reads only the CURRENT event" width="980">

Event id 6 has `et` = 220, so the naive watermark is 160. But `prev` is 200 and `seen` is already 260 — the event is out of order, and the formula has no memory of that. Note `seen` is correct and simply unused on this path.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 2 of 4</b> — so it goes BACKWARDS — 2 times</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch03-system-memory/frames/step-02.svg" alt="Step 2: so it goes BACKWARDS — 2 times" width="980">

`w` = -10 against `prev` = 160, so `back` reaches 2: 200 → 160 (−40s) and 160 → -10 (−170s). A watermark going backwards is not a cosmetic problem — the next step shows what it does to a window.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 3 of 4</b> — one line makes it monotonic</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch03-system-memory/frames/step-03.svg" alt="Step 3: one line makes it monotonic" width="980">

Same event, and `m` stays at 260 because `e.et` (220) is not greater. The emitted value is 200 — equal to the previous one, never below it. `back` stays 0 for the whole stream: 2 regressions become 0 by replacing `e.et` with `max(seen, e.et)`.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 4 of 4</b> — and a regression would UN-close a published window</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch03-system-memory/frames/step-04.svg" alt="Step 4: and a regression would UN-close a published window" width="980">

For window 0 the naive watermark reached 185 at index 4 — past 120, so the window fired and published. Then at index 7 it fell to -10, below 120 again. The window is now "not yet complete" after having been published. Nothing downstream has a concept for that.

</details>

<sub>Both formulas' outputs, the 2 regressions and the re-opened window are computed from the seed and asserted. Generated by `node tools/gen_ch03.js` on `tools/memkit.js`.</sub>
